guideTitle: 6 Best Wedge Pillows for Sitting Up in Bed in 2026
metaTitle: Best Wedge Pillows for Sitting Up (2026)
metaDescription: Six wedge and backrest pillows for sitting up in bed, compared by angle range, arm support, size and storage, for reading, TV and relaxing.
introParagraphs: Sitting up in bed is a different job from sleeping on an incline. You need a steeper angle, a wider back surface and often something for your arms and the things you reach for: a book, tablet, remote, glasses. Plain triangle wedges can do part of the job, but the best picks for this angle borrow ideas from reading pillows, with armrests, pockets and adjustable backs.

This lineup mixes three shapes. The Kayfia 30 to 90 Degree Adjustable Reading Pillow, ENITYA 22-Inch XL Reading Pillow and ENITYA 19-Inch Reading Pillow are armchair-style backrests. The Kölbs Wedge Reading Pillow with Arms is a firmer reading wedge. The IASEAHK Headboard Wedge Pillow spans the whole bed, and the Bedluxe Adjustable Wedge Pillow Set is a modular system for building your own slope.

These are comfort products for reading, television and relaxing, not medical devices. We evaluated them from specifications and buyer feedback, focusing on angle, stability and how much room they leave in the bed.

products.name: Kayfia 30 to 90 Degree Reading Pillow
products.description:
The Kayfia is the most adjustable pick for sitting up, with a stepless 30 to 90 degree angle control and a height range of 13.8 to 25.6 inches. Instead of choosing between a handful of fixed positions, you can slide to exactly the angle you like, from a gentle recline to a bolt-upright seat. For anyone who reads in one position and watches television in another, that range is the main draw.

The back is one piece of high-density, high-elasticity foam that the listing says resists sagging, and the arms use 26D support foam designed to bear arm weight without collapsing. A backrest with real arms is a different experience from a bare wedge, because it keeps your elbows supported over long reading sessions. It is also easier on the shoulders than propping on stacked pillows.

The tradeoff is size and complexity. A mechanism with a wide range has more parts than a solid wedge, and it takes up much more of the bed than the IASEAHK Headboard Wedge Pillow does at the head. It is also not meant for sleeping. If your main goal is a comfortable place to read and watch TV, though, it is the most flexible option here. Check that your mattress is wide enough to leave room for a partner before committing. Many buyers keep it on one side and use it only in the evening.
products.bestFor: People who read and watch TV at different angles.
pros: Wide height range of 13.8 to 25.6 inches
cons: Takes up a lot of bed space
More complex than a solid wedge

products.name: ENITYA 22-Inch XL Reading Pillow
products.description:
The ENITYA XL is a wide, armchair-style reading pillow with a fixed 60 degree ergonomic back angle and a multi-layer composite foam build. The listing describes each layer as carefully chosen for support and comfort, and the width at 22 inches gives you room to shift. The fixed 60 degree angle is steep, close to the angle of a comfortable armchair.

Its armrests and extra-large pockets are the practical stars. The pockets on both sides hold books, a phone, glasses or a remote, which saves a bedside trip and keeps things reachable. Compared with the Kölbs Wedge Reading Pillow with Arms, the pockets are bigger and the width is more generous, though the Kölbs highlights a solid foam core.

The angle is fixed, so you cannot adjust it the way you can on the Kayfia 30 to 90 Degree Reading Pillow. If 60 degrees feels too upright or too slouchy, there is nothing to change. It also takes real bed space. For those who sit up for long stretches and want roomy arms and storage, it is a comfortable pick.
products.bestFor: Long reading or TV sessions where arms and storage matter.
pros: Fixed 60 degree back angle feels armchair-like
cons: Takes up a lot of mattress space

products.name: Kölbs Wedge Reading Pillow with Arms
products.description:
The Kölbs reading wedge combines a wedge shape with arms, aimed at people who sit up in bed to read, game, watch television or nurse. The distinguishing detail is the solid foam core: the listing says it uses high-density solid foam instead of shredded fill, which tends to flatten and shift. Solid foam keeps the shape you bought.

That firmness is the reason to pick it. Shredded-fill backrests often sag by the second week, and the solid core addresses that complaint directly. It feels more structured than the ENITYA 22-Inch XL Reading Pillow, though it lacks the big storage pockets that ENITYA emphasizes.

The tradeoff is that a solid core is less adjustable and a bit less cushioned, and the angle is fixed. It is also not marketed as a sleeping wedge. If you want a firm, long-lasting backrest with armrests and prefer a clean design to a pocket-heavy one, this is a sensible choice.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want a firm solid-foam backrest with arms.
pros: Resists the flattening of shredded fill

products.name: IASEAHK Headboard Wedge Pillow
products.description:
The IASEAHK is the oddball in this lineup, because it is a headboard wedge: a long triangular backrest that spans the whole head of the bed. It comes in three sizes, with a Twin at 39 by 10 by 20 inches, a Queen at 59 by 10 by 20 inches and a King at 75 by 10 by 20 inches. It turns the headboard into a soft backrest so you can lean back anywhere along the bed.

The cover is dope-dyed polyester with a plush feel. The long shape is useful for couples because both people can lean back at the same time, without each needing their own pillow. It also stops pillows from slipping between the mattress and the headboard.

It does not give you armrests or adjustable angles, so it is the simplest backrest here. Compared with the Kayfia 30 to 90 Degree Reading Pillow it offers less flexibility but takes far less floor space. For households that want shared sitting-up comfort, it is the most practical. Setup is as easy as laying it along the headboard, with nothing to assemble. Make sure you order the size that matches your mattress width.
products.bestFor: Couples or anyone wanting a full-width headboard backrest.
pros: Spans the full head of the bed
Available in Twin, Queen and King sizes
Both people can lean back together
cons: Needs a headboard or wall behind it

products.name: ENITYA 19-Inch Reading Pillow
products.description:
The ENITYA 19-inch model is the smaller sibling of the XL, with the same idea of firm back support, fixed arms and enlarged side pockets in a narrower frame. At 19 inches wide it fits twin beds and shared queen beds without crowding, which makes it a good choice when bed space is tight.

The one-piece construction is the main upgrade the listing talks about: fixed arms provide steadier support than the floppy two-part reading pillows many shoppers have tried. The pockets are large enough to hold a book, remote or tablet. It is suited to reading, television and working from bed.

The smaller frame is a plus for compact spaces but a minus for larger bodies, who may find the back narrower than they want. It has a fixed angle, unlike the Kayfia 30 to 90 Degree Reading Pillow. For smaller beds, shared beds and lighter frames, it is the sweet spot. Taller readers may prefer the wider back of the ENITYA 22-Inch XL Reading Pillow. Both share the same pocket-first philosophy.
products.bestFor: Smaller beds and anyone who wants a narrower reading pillow.
pros: Compact 19 inch width fits tight beds

products.name: Bedluxe Adjustable Wedge Pillow Set
products.description:
The Bedluxe set is the only pick here that can serve both as a sitting-up backrest and as a sleeping wedge. Its 10-in-1 design lets you stack the pieces to reach 9 and 12 inches, and the dual-layer memory foam has a breathable top. That flexibility is useful if you want to sit up in the evening and lie back for the night.

It does not have the armrests or pockets of the ENITYA models, so the comfort of reading for hours depends more on the arrangement you build. The modular approach also takes more setup than a one-piece backrest. Unlike many modular sets, it lists clear heights, which helps planning.

It is a good compromise for a small bedroom where one set must do many jobs. If you only ever sit up and never sleep on a slope, the Kayfia or ENITYA pillows will feel more like an armchair. If you want one set to cover both, this is the one. It also packs away into separate pieces, so a guest room or small bedroom does not need to host a big backrest permanently. Treat it as a flexible sleeper-and-sitter rather than a dedicated reading chair.
products.bestFor: People who want a backrest by day and a sleeping wedge by night.
cons: More setup than a one-piece backrest
Shapes can shift if not braced

buyingCriteria.explanation: The right angle for sitting up in bed is much steeper than for sleeping. The ENITYA 22-Inch XL Reading Pillow uses a fixed 60 degree back, while the Kayfia 30 to 90 Degree Reading Pillow lets you choose anywhere between 30 and 90 degrees. Around 60 to 70 degrees feels like a comfortable armchair for most people. If you are unsure, choose an adjustable pillow so you can find your own angle.

Armrests turn a wedge into a chair. The Kölbs Wedge Reading Pillow with Arms and the ENITYA models include them, and the Kayfia lists 26D foam armrests designed to bear arm weight. Armrests keep your shoulders relaxed over long reading sessions. If you share the bed, check that the arms do not push into your partner's space.

Shredded-fill backrests tend to compress and shift over time, leaving you with a sagging pillow. The Kölbs lists a high-density solid foam core, and the Kayfia lists one-piece high-density foam. Solid foam costs more but keeps its shape. If you plan to use the pillow daily, favor solid foam.

These pillows can eat into the bed quickly. The ENITYA 19-Inch Reading Pillow is narrower than the ENITYA 22-Inch XL Reading Pillow, and the IASEAHK Headboard Wedge Pillow spans the width of the mattress in Twin, Queen or King. Measure your bed and decide how much space you can give up. In a shared bed, a narrower pillow or a full-width headboard wedge is easier to live with.

Pockets keep your remote, glasses and phone within reach. The ENITYA models have large pockets on both sides, while the Kölbs focuses on a cleaner shape. If you spend hours in bed, pockets quickly become the feature you use most. If you prefer a minimal look, skip them.

A sitting-up pillow needs a grippy base so it does not slide off the mattress. Check for a non-slip bottom, and look for a removable cover you can wash. The IASEAHK uses a breathable polyester cover, and the Bedluxe set uses a breathable memory foam top. A pillow that slides or cannot be washed will lose its appeal quickly.

howWeEvaluated.title: Angle and adjustability
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared fixed and adjustable angles, from the ENITYA 22-Inch XL Reading Pillow's 60 degrees to the Kayfia 30 to 90 Degree Reading Pillow's stepless range. We rewarded options that let you find your own seat angle, while recognizing that fixed designs are simpler. Where a listing gave no angle, we scored it more cautiously. We also noted that a steep angle with no way to change it can be a problem for people with stiff backs. A little adjustability was treated as a real benefit.

howWeEvaluated.title: Armrests and structure
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked whether each pillow has arms and what they are made of. The Kayfia lists 26D foam arms, the Kölbs lists a solid foam core, and the ENITYA models list fixed one-piece arms. Structures that keep their shape earned higher scores. We were wary of designs that rely on soft fill alone. A backrest has to survive daily use for months.

howWeEvaluated.title: Size and bed footprint
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed width and depth against typical mattress sizes. The ENITYA 19-Inch Reading Pillow suits compact beds, while the IASEAHK Headboard Wedge Pillow comes in sizes from Twin at 39 inches to King at 75 inches.

howWeEvaluated.title: Storage and convenience
howWeEvaluated.description: We gave credit for pockets, handles and washable covers, since these are daily conveniences. The ENITYA models lead on pockets.

howWeEvaluated.title: Lineup positioning
howWeEvaluated.description: The Kayfia leads on adjustability, the ENITYA 22-Inch XL on pockets and width, the Kölbs on solid foam, the IASEAHK on shared headboard use, the ENITYA 19-Inch on compact size and the Bedluxe on dual sleeping use. This is based on specifications and buyer feedback.

faq.q: What is the best angle for sitting up in bed?
faq.a: Around 60 to 70 degrees feels like a comfortable armchair for most people. The ENITYA 22-Inch XL Reading Pillow uses 60 degrees. If you want to try several angles, the Kayfia lets you adjust between 30 and 90 degrees.

faq.q: Can I sleep on a reading pillow?
faq.a: Most are designed for sitting, not sleeping. If you want a pillow for both, a modular wedge set such as the Bedluxe Adjustable Wedge Pillow Set can be arranged lower. Always follow your doctor's advice about sleep position.

faq.q: Why does my backrest pillow flatten?
faq.a: Shredded-fill pillows compress with use. Solid foam, as in the Kölbs Wedge Reading Pillow with Arms, resists this. Fluffing and rotating help but cannot fully restore shredded fill.

faq.q: Do I need a headboard wedge or a reading pillow?
faq.a: A headboard wedge fills the gap and gives a soft backrest across the whole bed, which suits couples. A reading pillow gives armrests and pockets for one person. Some people use both.

faq.q: How do I stop the pillow sliding down?
faq.a: Place it against the headboard or wall and choose one with a non-slip base. Fitted sheets with some texture help too. If it keeps sliding, a lower angle can make it more stable.
Many have removable covers, but you should check each listing. The IASEAHK uses a polyester cover, for example. The foam itself should not be machine washed.

faq.q: Will a sitting-up pillow fit my bed?
faq.a: Measure your mattress width and think about whether a partner shares it. The ENITYA 19-Inch Reading Pillow fits compact beds, and the IASEAHK comes in Twin, Queen and King sizes. Leave room to move.
